name: Unprotected shared write in parallel for
description: A shared variable is written inside a #pragma omp parallel for loop without any synchronization (no critical, atomic, or reduction clause). Multiple threads may write simultaneously, causing a data race.

name: Shared loop counter modification
description: The loop induction variable or an index variable is implicitly shared and modified inside a parallel region. OpenMP makes the loop variable private by default for parallel for, but auxiliary index variables may remain shared.

name: Indirect array access race
description: Array elements are accessed via an index set (indirect addressing) inside a parallel loop. If two iterations map to the same array index, a write-write or read-write race occurs. The compiler cannot prove disjointness at compile time.

name: Missing reduction clause
description: An accumulation pattern (sum, product, min, max) is performed in a parallel for loop using a shared variable with a compound assignment operator (+=, *=, etc.), but no reduction clause is specified.

name: Read-write race on shared scalar
description: One thread writes to a shared scalar variable while another thread reads it, without synchronization. Common with flag variables or status indicators.

name: Lock ordering violation (potential deadlock)
description: Two or more threads acquire multiple locks in different orders. Thread A holds lock1 and waits for lock2, while thread B holds lock2 and waits for lock1, causing a circular wait (deadlock).
symptoms: No CPU usage but no progress

name: Atomicity violation
description: A sequence of operations that should be atomic (check-then-act, read-modify-write) is interrupted by another thread between the check and the act. Each individual access may be synchronized, but the compound operation is not.

name: Python GIL misconception race
description: While CPython's GIL prevents true parallel execution of bytecodes, compound operations like list.append() in a tight loop or dict updates from multiple threads can still race because the GIL can be released between bytecodes of a compound operation.

name: Missing barrier synchronization
description: A parallel region computes values in one phase and uses them in a subsequent phase, but there is no barrier between the phases. Threads in the second phase may read values not yet written by threads in the first phase.
symptoms: Use of uninitialized or stale values

name: False sharing
description: Different threads write to different variables that happen to reside on the same cache line. This causes cache line bouncing between cores, severely degrading performance. Not a correctness bug, but a significant performance issue.

name: Unprotected shared collection in Python threads
description: A shared mutable collection (list, dict, set) is modified by multiple threads without a lock. While individual operations may be GIL-protected, sequences of operations (check-then-modify) are not atomic.
symptoms: RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration

name: Nowait on dependent loop
description: A #pragma omp for nowait is used on a loop whose results are consumed by a subsequent loop or code section. The nowait removes the implicit barrier, allowing threads to proceed before all iterations complete.
